idea: Cheap wrist wearable nudges the user with a single vibration pattern ninety minutes before their historically best bedtime, learned from a week of sleep-tracking data, with no app needed after the initial setup week.
source: hand-authored by Claude Sonnet 5, offline in this session, by-layer Slicer variant -- see foundry/tools/slicer.yaml

pieces.text: One week of sleep-tracking data is enough to reliably estimate a person's best bedtime, without needing months of data or accounting for weekday/weekend variation.
A single vibration pattern, ninety minutes ahead, is a strong enough cue that people will actually change behavior (start winding down) rather than ignore it like a phone notification.
A person's best bedtime stays stable enough week to week that a one-time, no-app-needed setup remains accurate for the device's useful life, rather than drifting out of date.
Removing the phone app after setup is a real selling point, rather than something that just removes a useful ongoing feedback loop and makes the device feel abandoned.
A device this narrow in function (one vibration, no app) can be priced cheaply enough that people buy it instead of using the sleep features already built into a phone or existing wearable they own.
